title: [Bug]: ripgrep ENOENT on Termux due to incompatible binary

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue report clearly describes a bug where grep_search fails on Termux (Android aarch64) with 'spawn .../rg ENOENT' due to attempting to execute a bundled ripgrep binary compiled for standard GNU/Linux (expecting /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1). The issue contains actionable reproduction details, platform specifics, root cause analysis, and expected behavior.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix requires adding environment detection for Termux, adjusting ripgrep binary resolution order to bypass glibc binaries on Termux, and updating system path validation to trust Termux binary locations. As a platform-specific issue involving child_process spawn behavior and non-FHS environment setups, this carries testing overhead across platform environments.

summary.problem: Gemini CLI fails to execute grep_search on Termux (Android aarch64) with 'spawn .../rg ENOENT' because the bundled ripgrep binary is compiled for standard GNU/Linux (glibc) and requires /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1.
summary.root_cause: resolveRipgrepPath() selects bundled rg-linux-arm64 on Termux because fileExists() returns true, even though the binary cannot execute in Termux's non-FHS environment. Furthermore, system PATH fallback fails because Termux binary paths like /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin are not included in isTrustedSystemPath().
summary.context: Termux is an Android terminal environment with a non-FHS filesystem hierarchy where binaries reside in /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin ($PREFIX/bin) and standard glibc dynamic linkers are absent.

steps: Add environment detection for Termux (e.g. checking process.env.TERMUX_VERSION or process.env.PREFIX) in packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.ts.
Update resolveRipgrepPath() in packages/core/src/tools/ripGrep.ts to skip bundled binaries when running under Termux, falling back to system PATH.
Update isTrustedSystemPath() in packages/core/src/utils/paths.ts to recognize Termux binary paths (such as process.env.PREFIX/bin or /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin) as trusted system paths.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When running in a Termux environment, resolveRipgrepPath() skips bundled glibc binaries and successfully resolves to the system-installed ripgrep executable in the Termux trusted path.
verification_steps: Mock Termux environment variables in resolveRipgrepPath() tests.
Verify that resolveRipgrepPath() skips bundled rg-linux-arm64 when Termux is detected.
Verify that isTrustedSystemPath() returns true for Termux system paths like /data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/rg.
